The answer is D - the foramen ovale. This is the structure that is supposed to form the fossa ovalis in adults. During fetal circulation, the foramen ovale allows blood to move from the placenta to the left atrium, bypassing the lungs. After birth, when the lungs start to inflate, this is no longer necessary and the septum primum and septum secundum meet to close the foramen ovale. In most people, it is completely closed in a few weeks after birth, but in some people it may remain partially or even completely open. This is known as a patent foramen ovale (PFO) and is usually harmless, although in some cases it can be associated with paradoxical emboli (where a clot in the legs travels through the PFO into the lungs) and heart murmur.

In times of infection, the mother's IgG levels will increase and therefore the foetus will have high levels of IgG present at birth. This provides the foetus with a degree of immunity after birth as the IgG can remain in the neonates circulation for the first few months of life.

The PaO2 value tells us that this patient is still hypoxaemic on 40% O2, which is worse than his baseline. This suggests that there has been a deterioration in his COPD, leading to hypercapnia. The PaCO2 value is low normal, which would suggest that the patient has hyperventilated to blow off CO2. However, the low PaCO2 is accompanied by a high HCO3- and a large base excess, which suggest that the patient has retained HCO3- due to renal compensation for metabolic acidosis. Therefore, the patient has respiratory acidosis compensated by metabolic alkalosis. This is a common presentation in patients with COPD who become hypercapnic and retain CO2. The body compensates by retaining HCO3- and excreting H+ in the urine.

Propranolol is a beta blocker and works by competitively inhibiting the actions of adrenaline and noradrenaline at beta 1 adrenoceptors found in cardiac tissue. This means that the heart is affected and hence propranolol is used to treat cardiac arrhythmias.

Vitamin A is also known as retinol and is found in carrots, leafy greens and liver. It is important for the rhodopsin pigment. Rhodopsin is a light-sensitive pigment found in the rod cells of the retina. It allows us to see in low light. Vitamin E can inhibit the function of Vitamin A.

The glenoid labrum is a fibrocartilaginous ring that surrounds the glenoid fossa of the scapula. It is formed from the deep cervical and subclavian branches of the cervical plexus. It is a rim of tissue that deepens the shallow glenoid fossa and increases the stability of the glenohumeral joint.
